correlation_analysis.analysis_summary: The analysis focused on mapping Windows Event IDs to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, prioritizing direct semantic matches and high confidence mappings. The most significant findings relate to credential access attempts via LSASS memory and NTDS database access. Several events related to LSASS process and shadow copy creation were mapped to credential access techniques. Events related to SYSVOL access and handle duplication were deemed too generic for confident mapping to the retrieved techniques.

direct_mappings.event_description: A new process has been created: C:\Windows\System32\ntdsutil.exe spawned by C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe with command line: ntdsutil  "ac i ntds" "ifm" "create full C:\Windows\Temp\ntds_T1003" q q
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: The event describes the use of ntdsutil.exe to create a full IFM backup of the Active Directory database (ntds.dit), which is a direct indicator of an attempt to access the NTDS database for credential extraction.
recommendations: Investigate the user account that initiated the cmd.exe process.
Examine the created IFM backup files in C:\Windows\Temp\ntds_T1003 for suspicious activity.
Monitor for further attempts to access or copy the ntds.dit file.

direct_mappings.event_description: lsass (600,G,0) Shadow copy instance 1 starting. This will be a Full shadow copy.
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: The event indicates the creation of a shadow copy for lsass.exe, which is a common technique used to dump credentials from LSASS memory.
recommendations: Investigate the process that initiated the shadow copy creation.
Monitor for subsequent access to the shadow copy volume.
Implement LSASS protection mechanisms to prevent credential dumping.
